title: Shared Inbox for Small Support Teams — Jon Martin
seoTitle: Shared Inbox Software for Small Support Teams
description: SupportBee, Help Scout, and Front compared for small support teams: per-seat prices, free plans and trials, HubSpot connections, and the limits to watch.
h1: A shared inbox for a small support team
dek: Three tools that turn support@ into a queue a small team can share, so every email gets one owner and one answer.
Prices and features below come from each vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown.

blocks.html: This is for a team of two to ten people answering customer email from a shared address, usually by forwarding and cc'ing each other, and losing track of who replied.
Many of these teams also keep customers in {{link:hubspot}}. The question is whether support conversations need to sit on that record, or whether a separate inbox is fine.

Pick SupportBee if you want a plain shared inbox at the lowest per-seat price. Pick Help Scout if you want to start on a free plan and grow into chat and a help center. Pick Front if the team lives in email and you want HubSpot contacts and deals visible beside each thread.
For a three-person team billed annually, that's about {{calc:supportbee_team3}} a month on SupportBee Startup, and about {{calc:front_team3}} on Front Starter.

SupportBee Startup is {{fact:supportbee.startup}}. Enterprise is {{fact:supportbee.enterprise}}. Per SupportBee, {{fact:supportbee.annual}}. Plans include {{fact:supportbee.unlimited}}, and Startup comes with {{fact:supportbee.kb}}. There's {{fact:supportbee.trial}}.
It's the most focused of the three: a shared inbox, a knowledge base, and the basics around them, without a long list of channels to configure.

Help Scout has {{fact:helpscout.free}}. Standard is {{fact:helpscout.standard}}, and it includes {{fact:helpscout.channels}}. Plus is {{fact:helpscout.plus}}. Plus also allows {{fact:helpscout.light_users}}.
Check the monthly and annual toggle on Help Scout's pricing page before you budget, since the figures above are what the default view shows.
Front Starter is {{fact:front.starter}}. Professional is {{fact:front.professional}}. Per Front, {{fact:front.annual}}. Starter gives you {{fact:front.starter_rules}}. There's {{fact:front.trial}}.
On HubSpot, Front offers {{fact:front.hubspot}}. That's the pick for a team that works deals and support out of the same inbox.
Start with seats. Count everyone who needs to reply, not everyone who needs to read. Some plans let teammates view without a full seat, and that changes the bill.
Then decide if support history belongs in HubSpot. If sales needs to see open tickets before a renewal call, a direct HubSpot connection is worth paying for. If not, keep it simple.
Last, look at the ceiling. Seat caps, automation rule limits, and knowledge base counts are what push a small team onto the next plan.
Write down three rules first: who owns a new email, how fast you reply, and when a thread counts as done. The tool enforces rules; it doesn't invent them.
Move one address at a time, and keep the old inbox forwarding for a few weeks so nothing slips through.

faq.q: Is there a free shared inbox?

faq.a: SupportBee Startup is {{fact:supportbee.startup}}. Front Starter is {{fact:front.starter}}.
Front offers {{fact:front.hubspot}}. Help Scout's Plus plan adds Salesforce, Jira, and HubSpot integrations.

closing: Agree on who owns each email first, then pick the cheapest inbox that enforces it and reaches HubSpot if you need it to.
